reason: An empty attribute set held by a 3.2.x pickle is left out of PROV-JSON and PROV-JSONLD output (#696, 3.3.0 pickle compatibility). It is the only test of the writers' empty-set skip.

Pins that a bare time string that does not parse raises with the position and the offending value (#555). The rows "usage", "invalidation", "start" and "end" went (8 items). `_decode_time` raises from one f-string with the position from `_position`, `_decode_formal_attribute` sends every relation's time to it, and `_decode_record_group` wraps only a ProvException, so the record type never enters the message. The rows "generation", "startTime" and "endTime" stay, each with both inputs.

A prefix a bundle declares for itself stays on that bundle after a read (#449). test_namespaces.py::test_a_namespace_a_bundle_registers_never_shadows_a_declared_prefix covers writer-side shadowing and never reads a bundle's own prefix object.
A bundle round trip writes no prefix inside the bundle and registers none on read (#449). The XML bundle-prefix tests cover another format.
A caller object_hook receives every object and the result equals a plain read (#532). The deserialize options promise on `ProvJSONSerializer` has no other test for object_hook.

A caller object_pairs_hook sees every pair, and a repeated key still raises before the hook sees it (#532). test_jsonld.py::test_deserialize_caller_object_pairs_hook_still_sees_every_pair covers the PROV-JSONLD reader, not this one.

`decode_json_container` rejects an integer record key through the guard in `_decode_record_group`. A caller object_pairs_hook can build such a dict. test_json.py::test_value_object_keys_a_caller_hook_makes_non_strings_are_rejected covers a different statement.

A non-ASCII character in a PROV-JSON string value survives deserialize. By default the writer escapes non-ASCII characters (json.dump's ensure_ascii), so the round trips of examples.py read only escapes, and this is the one test that gives the reader a raw non-ASCII character. No issue names it.

A "" prefix and a "default" key that agree read, and ones that disagree raise "two different default namespaces". Without it, the check in `decode_json_container` could be dropped, or made to reject agreeing keys, and no other test would notice.
A "" prefix declares the default namespace on read. The JSON-LD test covers another reader.

`encode_json_container` called with no prefix map declares both "default" and "dn" for a default namespace (#517). The sibling prefix-map test always passes a map, so only this test covers the no-map branch.

Pins the present result of the fallback branch of `ProvJSONEncoder.default`, which returns the JSON text of a plain string it is called with. The branch calls the superclass's encode where the docstring promises its default handling, so `json.dumps` with this encoder raises RecursionError for a value it cannot encode, where plain json raises TypeError (#786). The assertion misses that reachable case. The test changes with the fix to assert the TypeError.
Two equal anonymous relations write under one _:id1 key and read back as two records. No issue names the contract, but no other test covers the shared-key write.
A formal attribute under two keys with equal values reads as one value (#774). The two rows differ in arcs (formal and member paths), and the rejecting sibling uses different values.
Every record of a hadMember fan-out carries the identifier and attributes (#530). It compares the fan-out with one membership per member, so it is also the strictest check of member resolution.

A member listed twice in a hadMember array yields one record (#700). test_jsonld.py::test_deserialize_membership_entity_array_gives_one_record_per_member (row a-member-twice) covers the PROV-JSONLD reader, not this one.
A hadMember array with no collection warns once and builds no record (#710, spec 5 section 4.6). No other test covers the fan-out with a missing collection.

A one-element prov:entity array on a hadMember reads as the bare string (#530, #531). It is the length-one input, separate from the several-member fan-out tests, and the JSON-LD test covers another reader.

Proposed for deletion and kept. Document equality compares record sets, so the fan-out test cannot see record order, and the repeated-member test writes its members already sorted. A fan-out that sorts, or dedupes through a set, in `_add_memberships` passes both, and `_decode_members` documents "in the order written". Ruled rewrite, because the maintainer ruled that the order of the hadMember records `_add_memberships` builds is not a contract, so the order the test pins is incidental. The rewrite compares the members without their order. Later audit: rewrite it that way, or propose it for removal with the order ruling as the ground.

A hadMember with prov:entity written before prov:collection still fans out to one record per member (#275, cited in the test). The fixture and the writer both put the collection first, so only this test covers the reverse key order.
json.loads with cls=`ProvJSONDecoder` returns the same document as deserialize, as the class docstring promises. No other test uses the decoder class directly.
A value typed prov:QUALIFIED_NAME still reads as a QualifiedName, so 2.x output keeps parsing (#168). The reader tests with xsd:QName check neither the legacy type nor the value.

Proposed for deletion and kept. No other test sends several values to prov:entity of a non-membership record, and prov:entity has its own list branch in `_decode_record_instance`, so a first-value carve-out there (#531) would pass every other test.

For every example, in json and jsonld key modes, `_JSONPrefixMap` writes str(name) and declares the namespaces as 3.2.2 did (#517, #518), so output for documents without a default namespace stays unchanged. The json and jsonld rows assert different default keys, so both stay.
A QualifiedName value writes as a value object typed xsd:QName (#168). No other test checks the writer's datatype.

Seven rows were proposed for removal. Six were kept. Rows "repeated record" and "repeated value-object key" are separate defects in #532 and sit at different decode levels, so a rewrite that checks for repeated keys at each level, to give the message a position, could miss either of them. Rows "array time value object", "array collection", "undeclared datatype with lang" and "formal attribute full IRI with a space" each reach a branch no other row reaches. Row "formal float" was dropped, a JSON float against the int of row "formal number". `_decode_record_instance` and `_decode_formal_attribute` branch only on the attribute and on a list, and `_decode_name` rejects every non-string at one guard with one template filled by `_json_text`, so the type difference blocks nothing. Row "formal number" keeps #597 pinned, and row "float typed int" catches a float-specific `_json_text` fault. The only separating fault, an `isinstance(value, (int, dict))` guard, is contrived.
Three records with one identifier serialise to one list and read back as three. It covers the append branch of the writer for the third and later record.

Pins that a time written as an xsd:dateTime value object reads like the bare string (#554, which promises this for every relation's time). Rows "usage", "invalidation", "start" and "end" went. `_decode_record_group` only looks the record type up, the one record-type branch in `_decode_record_instance` is the hadMember test, and `_decode_formal_attribute` sends every relation's time to `_decode_time`, so the "generation" row pins the value-object path for every relation. If one of these gains a record-type branch, the check flags this row and the four rows may be needed again. The per-relation time round trips in test_statements.py catch a model-side fault. The rows "generation", "startTime" and "endTime" stay, one per time attribute name.

`decode_json_representation` called with no record or attribute gives the message with no position, as its docstring says, and `_check_value_object` builds that message. No other test covers that call.
A hook that turns a value-object key into an int gives the unknown-key error (#529). It reaches the sorted(..., key=str) path in `_check_value_object` that no row of the reject test reaches.
A JSON number in a value object typed xsd:int, xsd:long or xsd:double reads as its string form (#529), as 2.x and 1.x wrote it. The rows "double" and "double-with-exponent" assert different text.
With parse_float=Decimal, a numeric value-object $ is rejected (#529). test_value_forms.py::test_json_number_read_as_decimal_is_stored_as_a_literal covers only a bare number, which is accepted.

Seven valid attribute value forms read without error (#528, #529, #552), so the reader does not over-reject. The round trips read only what the writer produces, while this test feeds hand-written forms one by one, so a reader that rejects one of them fails here with the form named.
